milestone: Alpha 1.72 network jump input and floor authority
status: partial prepared implementation; not versioned or published as 1.72
baselineEvidence: The isolated dungeon_jump-input test failed on the preceding source: a network jump used client targetY=999 as its airborne landing height.
implementation: Reject nonfinite and float32-overflowing X/Y/Z before changing network jump state, including finite JSON-representable overflow values.
Reject network restart/redirection while the actor is already jumping. The server's current flight progress and target remain unchanged.
Keep landing height on the server-owned floor or resolve overworld destination terrain. Existing casino, geometry, recovery context, movement-lock and crowd-control rules remain.
Trusted internal jump helpers retain their previous admission behavior; no arbitrary distance cap or changed flight duration was silently added.

verification.newCases: Seven invalid-coordinate cases preserve idle/flight state; overworld, canonical dungeon and shared Dark Realm cases accept ordinary horizontal jumps while ignoring client targetY=999, then reject mid-flight restart without changing progress, destination or duration.
verification.retainedCases: Existing canonical jump destination, server-tick flight/landing and dead-jump checks; all six WorldGrounding groups; network walking allowance/path/height checks; rock sequencing/grounding; town recovery and shared expedition context reset passed.

limits: Arbitrary-distance jumps still use the prior capped flight time. Owner choice between quick range-limited jumps and distance-scaled flight was requested; the full jump movement trust boundary is not closed.

These checks do not constitute a connected browser/socket jump route, campaign, PvP anti-cheat certification, capacity soak, production binary or deployment. Existing source receipts remain historical for their recorded hashes.
No live characters, saved stats, production services, host settings or credentials were changed. Ordered predecessor releases and the remaining 1.71/1.72 requirements remain open.
